retention_rule: A judge seeking retention needs at least 60% 'Yes' votes from those voting on that judge to keep the seat. Circuit judges serve 6-year terms and appellate judges 10-year terms. Judges do not run against one another; each is a separate Yes/No question. (Injustice Watch; Chicago Bar Association.)

gap_247: Ballot #247/#248 was Judge John J. Mahoney (III), Circuit Court, Fifth Municipal District (Bridgeview). His Injustice Watch profile says: "Mahoney withdrew from the retention election in September, after the State Board of Election ballot certification deadline. Due to the timing, his name will still appear on the ballot, but votes for or against him will not be counted." The CBA's 2026 list skips #247 (Kuzas #245, then Martinez #249), and neither the CBA, CCL nor Alliance PDF evaluates him. The ISBA-hosted Alliance grid lists him with all Yes, apparently from before he withdrew. No reason for the withdrawal was found. Background: he was retained in 2020 with 60.1%, after ISBA declined to recommend him over attorneys' concerns about "arrogance and a lack of sensitivity to diversity issues" (Injustice Watch, 2020). Depending on how the printed ballot was prepared, his name may still appear at #247/248; votes cast there will not count.
